mainTopic: זוגות (the danger of 'pairs'): when even numbers are dangerous, how many cups are safe, and remedies against demons and witches
overview: This amud is about זוגות, the danger of doing things in even numbers. It opens by finishing an earlier answer: each of the ארבע כוסות is its own מצוה, so they do not form a pair. אביי then explains a ברייתא about marital relations: after eating or drinking in pairs, one should not have relations even once, because it weakens him. A ברייתא warns that one who drinks כפלים is responsible for his own harm. The גמרא then limits this: going out to see the marketplace between cups breaks the pair, and the danger applies mainly when setting out on the road, going to sleep, or going to the בית הכסא. Sages who were careful even at home are explained as a special case, because an אדם חשוב is different. Next, several opinions argue about where the danger stops. עולא says ten cups are safe. Others use the words of ברכת כהנים to make eight, six, and even four safe, and רבא acted on this view. Reports from יוסף שידא describe אשמדאי as ruling over pairs and explain when two or four cups can harm. The גמרא gives a remedy of counting with one's thumbs for someone who went out after a pair. It then begins אמימר's protective formula against witches, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Each cup at the סדר is its own separate מצוה
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes the previous answer: the ארבע כוסות are not a dangerous pair, because each cup is a separate מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Each cup is a separate מצוה on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer on the previous amud. It explains why drinking four cups at the סדר is not the dangerous 'pairs' problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that four cups is an even number, which would be a זוגות problem. The answer is that each cup is its own separate מצוה, so the cups are not counted together as pairs.

keyTerms.meaning: A separate מצוה standing on its own

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not begin a new topic. It is the end of an answer that started on the previous amud, about the ארבע כוסות.

phrases.english: It is a מצוה in its own right.
phrases.notes: Each of the four cups stands alone, so they are not counted together as pairs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer that began on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition: each cup is counted separately, not as part of a group
steps.terutzMaskana: The ארבע כוסות do not create a זוגות problem.

steps.title: Why should unplanned marital relations count as a pair?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא that says not to have marital relations in pairs, since a second time is not planned in advance.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: 'One should not attend to his needs in pairs.' Why? He changed his mind!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא about pairs and asks why it applies. The person did not plan to do it twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption here is that two acts only join into a 'pair' when they are planned together. A second act of relations is a new decision (נמלך), so it should not join with the first.

keyTerms.meaning: His needs (a polite way to refer to marital relations)
He reconsidered and made a new decision

phrases.english: "One should not attend to his needs in pairs":
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא being discussed.

phrases.english: Why? He changed his mind!
phrases.notes: The second time is a new decision, so it should not join the first to make a pair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to another line of the same ברייתא about pairs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unplanned acts are not counted together, so a second act of relations should not make a pair.

steps.title: אביי: after eating or drinking in pairs, avoid relations even once
steps.stepSummary: אביי reinterprets the ברייתא: it is not about doing relations twice. Rather, after eating or drinking in pairs, one should not have relations at all, because it weakens him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what it means. One should not eat in pairs or drink in pairs. And if he did, he should not attend to his needs even once, in case he becomes weak and is harmed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by explaining the ברייתא differently. The danger comes from food or drink taken in pairs, and relations afterward make it worse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'pair' is no longer the two acts of relations; it is the pair of foods or drinks. Relations matter only because the weakness they cause leaves the person open to the harm of the pair. This avoids the problem of a second act that was never planned.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a reinterpretation of the source)
He is harmed or suffers misfortune

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what it is saying:
One should not eat in pairs or drink in pairs,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יַעֲשֶׂה צְרָכָיו אֲפִילּוּ פַּעַם אַחַת —
phrases.english: and he should not attend to his needs even once,
phrases.notes: This applies after he has eaten or drunk in pairs.

phrases.english: lest he become weak and be harmed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids doing relations twice.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא forbids relations even once after eating or drinking in pairs, because of weakness.

steps.title: One who drinks in pairs bears responsibility for himself
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one who drinks כפלים is responsible for whatever harm comes to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One who drinks in pairs, his blood is on his own head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with a strong warning against drinking an even number of cups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'His blood is on his head' means that if he is harmed, it is his own fault. The next steps will narrow down when this danger actually applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Double, an even number of cups
His blood is on his own head (he is responsible for his own harm)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One who drinks in pairs,
his blood is on his own head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source on the same topic of pairs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drinking an even number of cups is dangerous, and the drinker is responsible for his own harm.

steps.title: רב יהודה: seeing the marketplace breaks the pair
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה limits the ברייתא: the danger applies only if he did not go out and see the marketplace between cups.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: When does this apply? When he did not see the marketplace. But if he saw the marketplace, he is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה adds a limit to the ברייתא. Going outside between cups 'breaks' the pair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cups only join into a pair if they are drunk as one continuous sitting. Going out to the marketplace separates them, so the second cup starts fresh.

keyTerms.meaning: When? (introduces a limit to a ruling)
The face of the marketplace (going outside)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: When does this apply?
When he did not see the marketplace;
but if he saw the marketplace,
he has permission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Going out to the marketplace between cups breaks the pair.

steps.title: רב אשי saw רב חנניא בר ביבי go out after each cup
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that רב חנניא בר ביבי would go out and look at the marketplace after every cup, which supports רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I saw רב חנניא בר ביבי. On each cup he would go out and look at the marketplace.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי tells what an אמורא actually did. This shows that רב יהודה's rule was followed in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real practice (מעשה רב) supports the idea that seeing the marketplace breaks the pair. רב חנניא did this after each cup so that no two cups would join together.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: I saw
Rav Chananya bar Bivi
that on each cup he would go out
and look at the marketplace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה with an example of practice.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's rule that seeing the marketplace breaks the pair
steps.raayaSupportSource: What רב חנניא בר ביבי did, as רב אשי saw it

steps.title: The danger applies only when setting out on the road
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the danger of pairs to someone about to travel, not someone staying home.
steps.simpleTranslation: We said this only for one going out on the road. But at home, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another limit. The danger of drinking in pairs applies when one is about to set out on a journey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A traveler is more exposed to harm, so the danger of pairs matters there. At home, the גמרא at first says there is no concern.

keyTerms.meaning: We said this only... (a limiting formula)
To set out on the road

phrases.english: And we said this only for one setting out on the road,
but in his home, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another limit to the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The danger of pairs applies to one leaving for the road, not to one staying home.

steps.title: רבי זירא: going to sleep is like setting out on the road
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says that one who goes to sleep after drinking in pairs is in danger, just like a traveler.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Going to sleep is like setting out on the road.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא widens the 'road' category to include going to sleep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though sleeping happens at home, a sleeping person is unprotected in the same way a traveler is. So the danger of pairs applies.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: And going to sleep
is like setting out on the road.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the 'road' category from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sleeping after drinking in pairs is treated like traveling, so the danger applies.

steps.title: רב פפא: going to the bathroom is like setting out on the road
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא adds that going to the בית הכסא also counts like going out on the road.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Going to the בית הכסא is like setting out on the road.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds one more case to the 'road' category.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outhouses were outside and were considered dangerous places, so going there is like traveling. The danger of pairs applies.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: וְלָצֵאת לְבֵית הַכִּסֵּא —
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: And going out to the bathroom
is like setting out on the road.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: וְלָצֵאת לְבֵית הַכִּסֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case to the 'road' category, after רבי זירא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Going to the בית הכסא after drinking in pairs is treated like traveling.

steps.title: But רבא counted the beams to avoid pairs even at home
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that home is safe: רבא counted the beams of his house to make sure he did not drink an even number of cups.
steps.simpleTranslation: And at home there is no concern? But רבא would count the beams!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 7, which said there is no danger at home. רבא was careful about pairs even inside his house, which suggests home is not safe. Step 11 adds more examples to this challenge, and step 12 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If staying home were safe, רבא would not have needed to count beams to track his cups. His practice contradicts the rule that the danger applies only on the road.

phrases.english: And at home there is no concern?
But Rava would count beams!
phrases.notes: He used the beams to keep track of how many cups he drank, to avoid an even number.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְבֵיתוֹ לָא? וְהָא רָבָא מָנֵי כְּשׁוּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit stated in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule 'אבל בביתו לא' (no danger at home)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא was careful about pairs at home, so the danger must apply at home too.

steps.title: More stories of great people guarding against pairs at home
steps.stepSummary: The challenge continues. אביי's mother and רב נחמן בר יצחק's attendant made sure these sages never stopped at an even number of cups, even at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי: when he drank one cup, his mother would put two cups in his two hands. And רב נחמן בר יצחק: when he drank two cups, his attendant would hand him one more cup. If he drank one cup, the attendant would put two cups in his two hands!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still attacking the idea that pairs are only dangerous when traveling. It brings two more stories of sages who were careful at home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said the danger of pairs applies only to someone about to travel. Step 10 brought רבא counting beams at home to challenge this. Now the stories of אביי and רב נחמן בר יצחק add to that challenge, since both were careful to avoid an even number even while sitting at home.

keyTerms.meaning: His mother (here, the woman who raised אביי)

phrases.english: And Abaye, when he would drink one cup,

phrases.aramaic: מְנַקֵּיט לֵיהּ אִימֵּיהּ תְּרֵי כָסֵי בִּתְרֵי יְדֵיהּ.
phrases.english: his mother would place two cups in his two hands.
phrases.notes: So he would end up with an odd total of three, not two.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, כִּי הֲוָה שָׁתֵי תְּרֵי כָסֵי,
phrases.english: And Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak, when he would drink two cups,
his attendant would place one cup in his hand,
phrases.notes: So the total becomes three, an odd number.

phrases.aramaic: חַד כָּסָא — מְנַקֵּיט לֵיהּ תְּרֵי כָסֵי בִּתְרֵי יְדֵיהּ!
phrases.english: and after one cup, he would place two cups in his two hands!
phrases.notes: The exclamation shows this is part of the challenge: they were careful even at home.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds two more cases to the challenge of step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from step 7 that pairs are dangerous only for someone about to travel.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Great sages were careful about pairs while staying home, so home must not be safe.

steps.title: An important person is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that important people need extra care, so their behavior does not prove that ordinary people are in danger at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: An important person is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of steps 10–11 in three words. These sages were special cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule still stands: for an ordinary person, the danger of pairs applies mainly when going out. An important person draws more attention from the harmful forces, so he must be careful even at home. The stories show a stricter standard for great people, not the basic rule for everyone.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that home is dangerous for everyone. The stories describe a stricter level of care only for an אדם חשוב.

phrases.english: An important person is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge raised in steps 10–11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the cases involved special people.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sages' carefulness at home proves home is dangerous for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an אדם חשוב needs this extra care at home. For an ordinary person, the rule of step 7 stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The danger of pairs is mainly for someone going out. An אדם חשוב must be careful even at home.

steps.title: Ten cups do not count as a dangerous pair
steps.stepSummary: עולא says that drinking ten cups carries no danger of pairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Ten cups have no problem of pairs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question: do large even numbers still count as dangerous pairs? עולא says ten is safe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we assumed every even number is dangerous. עולא introduces a limit: at ten, the danger of pairs no longer applies. This opens a list of opinions about where the danger stops.

keyTerms.meaning: Pairs (even numbers, thought to be dangerous)
They do not contain the problem of

phrases.english: Ulla said:

phrases.aramaic: עֲשָׂרָה כּוֹסוֹת אֵין בָּהֶם מִשּׁוּם זוּגוֹת.
phrases.english: Ten cups have no element of pairs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: עֲשָׂרָה כּוֹסוֹת אֵין בָּהֶם מִשּׁוּם זוּגוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the upper limit of the danger of pairs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ten cups are not considered a dangerous pair.

steps.title: עולא's proof from the ten cups in a mourner's house
steps.stepSummary: עולא's view fits his other teaching: the חכמים instituted ten cups in the בית האבל. They would never set up something dangerous, so ten must be safe. Eight, though, is still a dangerous pair.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא follows his own reasoning. עולא said, and some say a ברייתא taught: The חכמים instituted ten cups in the house of a mourner. If you think ten cups do count as pairs, how could the רבנן set up something that leads to danger?! But eight cups do count as pairs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where עולא's opinion comes from. It is based on the ten cups of wine the חכמים set up for the mourner's meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is simple: the חכמים would never require something dangerous, so ten cups cannot be a dangerous pair. This proof only covers ten. Eight was never instituted, so for עולא eight is still dangerous. That last line sets up the next opinions, which argue about eight and six.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it would enter your mind (if you were to think)

phrases.english: Ulla follows his own reasoning,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר עוּלָּא, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא:
phrases.english: as Ulla said, and some say it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: עֲשָׂרָה כּוֹסוֹת תִּיקְּנוּ חֲכָמִים בְּבֵית הָאֵבֶל,
phrases.english: The Sages instituted ten cups in the house of a mourner,
and if you would think

phrases.aramaic: עֲשָׂרָה כּוֹסוֹת יֵשׁ בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם זוּגוֹת,
phrases.english: that ten cups do have the element of pairs,
how could the Sages arise and institute
something that leads to danger?!

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל תְּמָנְיָא יֵשׁ בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם זוּגוֹת.
phrases.english: But eight do have the element of pairs.
phrases.notes: This limits עולא's rule and sets up the next opinions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and reasoning behind עולא's ruling in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: עולא's claim that ten cups are not a dangerous pair.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The institution of ten cups in the בית האבל. The חכמים would not institute something dangerous.

steps.title: Eight is also safe because of the word שלום
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא say the seventh cup, matched to the word שלום in ברכת כהנים, joins the earlier cups only for good. So eight is safe, but six is still dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא both say: "שלום" joins for good, but does not join for bad. But six cups do count as pairs.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion lowers the safe limit from ten to eight. The reason comes from the word שלום in ברכת כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third verse of ברכת כהנים has seven words and ends with שלום, a purely good word. So the seventh cup counts toward blessing, not toward harm. That makes eight safe. Six has no such protection, so six is still dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace; the seventh word of the last verse of ברכת כהנים

steps.confusionAlert: The word שלום is not said over the cups. It is a sign from the number of words in the פסוק, showing that the number seven is good, so counting past it is not harmful.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda and Rabbah bar Rav Huna, who both say:
"Shalom" joins for good,
phrases.notes: שלום is the seventh word of the third verse of ברכת כהנים (במדבר ו:כו).

phrases.english: but does not join for bad.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שִׁיתָּא יֵשׁ בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם זוּגוֹת.
phrases.english: But six do have the element of pairs.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with עולא's limit of ten and lowers the safe point to eight.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eight cups are not a dangerous pair, but six are.

steps.title: Six is also safe because of the word ויחנך
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף say the fifth cup, matched to the word ויחנך in ברכת כהנים, joins only for good. So six is safe, but four is still dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: "ויחנך" joins for good, but does not join for bad. But four cups do count as pairs.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion lowers the safe limit even more, to six. The reason comes from the word ויחנך in ברכת כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second verse of ברכת כהנים has five words and ends with ויחנך, a word of grace. So the fifth cup counts only toward good. That makes six safe. Only four, and smaller even numbers, remain dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: "And be gracious to you"; the fifth word of the second verse of ברכת כהנים

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on where the danger of pairs stops. עולא says ten is safe and eight is dangerous. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא say eight is safe because of שלום, and six is dangerous. רבה and רב יוסף say six is safe because of ויחנך, and four is dangerous.

phrases.english: Rabbah and Rav Yosef, who both say:
"Vichuneka" joins for good.
phrases.notes: ויחנך is the fifth word of the second verse of ברכת כהנים (במדבר ו:כה).

phrases.english: For bad, it does not join.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַרְבָּעָה יֵשׁ בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם זוּגוֹת.
phrases.english: But four do have the element of pairs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same method as step 15 but lowers the safe limit from eight to six.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Six cups are not a dangerous pair, but four are.

steps.title: אביי and רבא: The Third Cup Joins Only for Good
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא say the word וישמרך, the third word of ברכת כהנים, joins for good but not for bad. So even four cups are safe.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both say: "וישמרך" joins for good, but it does not join for bad.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last and most lenient link in the chain of opinions. אביי and רבא say that even four cups carry no danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the fifth cup (ויחנך) was said to join only for good, which made six safe but left four dangerous. Here the third cup, matched to וישמרך, also joins only for good and not for bad. So the count toward a harmful pair is broken at the third cup, and a fourth cup does not complete a dangerous pair.

keyTerms.meaning: "And He will guard you". The third word of ברכת כהנים, matched here to the third cup.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think אביי and רבא are saying four is a 'good pair'. They are saying the third cup does not count toward forming a harmful pair. So four never adds up to a dangerous even number.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the most lenient view in the list: even four ordinary cups carry no danger of זוגות. The ארבע כוסות of the סדר were already explained on separate grounds in step 1, because each cup is its own מצוה.

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava, who both say:
"And He will guard you" (the third word)
phrases.notes: This word goes with the third cup.

phrases.english: for good, it joins;
for bad, it does not join.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the pattern of steps 15–16 one level lower, from the fifth cup to the third. This makes four cups safe.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third cup (וישמרך) joins only for good, so four cups are not a dangerous pair.

steps.title: רבא Acted on His View with Four Cups
steps.stepSummary: רבא's practice matches his teaching: he let the רבנן go home after drinking four cups.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא follows his own reasoning, because רבא sent the רבנן out after four cups.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבא really lived by his opinion. He let the רבנן leave after drinking four cups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If four cups were dangerous, רבא would not have sent people out into the street after drinking four. His action proves that he truly held four cups to be safe.

keyTerms.meaning: And he follows his own reasoning (consistent with his other view)
He sent them out / let them leave

phrases.english: And Rava follows his own reasoning,
for Rava sent the Sages out
after four cups,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's half of step 17 with his real-life practice.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that four cups are not dangerous
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's practice of letting the רבנן leave after four cups

steps.title: רבא Explains Away רבא בר ליואי's Injury
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר ליואי was once hurt after four cups. רבא did not blame the cups. He said the injury came because רבא בר ליואי had challenged him during the public lecture.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though רבא בר ליואי was hurt, רבא did not worry about it. He said: that happened because he challenged me during the lecture.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone could object: one of those רבנן actually got hurt, so four cups must be dangerous after all. The גמרא answers that רבא gave a different cause for the injury.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The injury looks like evidence against רבא's view. רבא says it was a punishment for a different wrong. רבא בר ליואי had raised a difficulty against his rebbe during the public lecture, which is disrespectful. So the injury does not prove that four cups are harmful.

keyTerms.meaning: He was not concerned about the matter
He challenged me / raised an objection against me

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיתַּזַּק רָבָא בַּר לֵיוַאי,
phrases.english: Even though Rava bar Livai was injured,
he (Rava) was not concerned about the matter,
for he said: that was because
he challenged me during the lecture.
phrases.notes: It is improper to embarrass one's rebbe in public.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיתַּזַּק רָבָא בַּר לֵיוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the proof in step 18 against a hidden objection: someone did get hurt.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different cause for the harm
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The injury of רבא בר ליואי after four cups would show that four is a dangerous pair.
steps.terutzMaskana: The injury was a punishment for challenging his rebbe in public, not a result of the four cups.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי and רבא, four cups are safe. רבא even acted on this, and he explained away the one injury as having a different cause.

steps.title: אשמדאי Rules Over Pairs, and a King Does Not Harm
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reports that יוסף שידא told him: אשמדאי, king of the demons, is in charge of all pairs. A king is not called a damager, so pairs are not dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: יוסף the demon told me: אשמדאי, king of the demons, is appointed over all pairs, and a king is not called a damager.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new piece of information about pairs that came straight from a demon. It suggests that pairs may not be dangerous at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The demon who controls pairs is the king himself. A king acts with dignity and does not go around causing small harms. So there is no reason to fear harm from doing things in pairs.

keyTerms.meaning: יוסף the demon, who gave information to the חכמים

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Yosef the demon told me:
Ashmedai, king of the demons,
is appointed over all pairs,
and a king is not called a damager.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, אָמַר לִי יוֹסֵף שֵׁידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the count-of-cups discussion and brings a new report about who controls pairs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pairs are under the king of demons, and a king does not cause harm.

steps.title: Other Version: The King Does Whatever He Wants
steps.stepSummary: Another version reverses the point. Since אשמדאי is an angry king, he can do as he pleases, just as a king may break through a fence to make a road and no one may stop him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it the other way: On the contrary, he is an angry king who does what he wants. A king may break through a fence to make himself a road, and no one may protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רב יוסף's report. It reaches the opposite conclusion: pairs are very dangerous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree that אשמדאי is in charge of pairs. They argue about what being a king means. The first version says a king is too dignified to harm. This version says a king has full power and no one can hold him back. It uses the הלכה that a king may break a fence for his road as a picture of that power.

keyTerms.meaning: In this direction, the opposite way
No one may protest against him

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions agree on the fact that אשמדאי rules over pairs. They only disagree about whether that makes pairs safe or dangerous.

phrases.english: Some say it in this other direction:
On the contrary, he is an angry king,
who does whatever he wants,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ פּוֹרֵץ גָּדֵר לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ דֶּרֶךְ
phrases.english: for a king may break through a fence to make himself a road
and no one may protest against him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposite version of step 20's report.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: As an all-powerful king, אשמדאי may harm those who do things in pairs.

steps.title: רב פפא: Two Can Kill, Four Only Harms
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא reports from יוסף שידא that two cups can lead to death, while four cups do not kill but can still harm.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: יוסף the demon told me: For two, we kill. For four, we do not kill, but for four, we harm.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report from the same demon. It describes different levels of danger for two cups and four cups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This report says the danger gets smaller as the pair number grows, but it does not disappear. Two cups is the most serious, with a risk of death. Four is milder, with a risk of harm but not death.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Yosef the demon told me:
With two, we kill;
with four, we do not kill;
with four, we harm.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, אָמַר לִי יוֹסֵף שֵׁידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another report from יוסף שידא, this time about levels of danger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two cups risk death. Four cups risk harm, but not death.

steps.title: רב פפא: With Four, Only Doing It on Purpose Matters
steps.stepSummary: Another difference between two and four: two is dangerous whether done by accident or on purpose. Four is dangerous only if done on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: With two, it applies whether by accident or on purpose. With four, if on purpose, yes; if by accident, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא continues the demon's report with a second difference between two cups and four cups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two cups the danger is complete: even someone who did not notice he drank a pair is at risk. With four, the demons only harm someone who drinks the pair deliberately. Someone who drinks four by accident is not harmed.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on pairs here. אביי and רבא say four cups are safe. יוסף שידא, through רב יוסף, reports that אשמדאי rules over pairs, with two versions of whether that is safe or dangerous. Through רב פפא, he reports that two cups is very dangerous while four is less so, and four is only dangerous when done on purpose.

phrases.english: With two, whether by accident or on purpose.
With four, on purpose, yes;
by accident, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב פפא's report with a second difference between two and four.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two cups is dangerous even by accident. Four cups is dangerous only when done on purpose.

steps.title: What if he forgot and went outside after a pair?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what remedy exists for someone who forgot and went outside after drinking an even number of cups.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he forgot, and it happened that he went outside, what is his remedy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question: what can a person do if he went out after drinking a pair of cups? This sets up the remedy that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא discussed when pairs are dangerous. Step 23 said that two cups are dangerous even when done by accident. So the case of someone who forgot is exactly the case that needs a solution, and the גמרא now looks for one.

phrases.english: And if he forgot
and it happened that he went outside
phrases.notes: He went out after drinking an even number of cups.

phrases.english: what is his remedy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from Step 23, which said a pair of two is dangerous even by accident. Now the גמרא asks how to protect someone who made that mistake.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical fix for someone already exposed to the danger of זוגות.

steps.title: Hold your thumbs and count to three
steps.stepSummary: He holds each thumb in the opposite hand and says: you and I make three, so he is no longer a pair.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should take his right thumb in his left hand and his left thumb in his right hand, and say: 'You and I make three.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the remedy. The person holds his two thumbs and declares that the thumbs plus himself make three, an odd number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger comes from the number being even. By counting his two thumbs together with himself, he turns the total into three. That way he is no longer standing as a 'pair'.

phrases.english: Let him take his own right thumb
in his left hand
and his left thumb in his right hand,
and say as follows:
'You and I, that makes three.'
phrases.notes: 'You' means the two thumbs. With the person himself, the total is three, which is not a pair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Grasp the thumbs crosswise and declare 'you and I are three', turning the even count into an odd one.

steps.title: If the demon answers back, keep counting odd
steps.stepSummary: If he hears a voice say 'four', he answers 'five'. If it says 'six', he answers 'seven'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he hears it say 'You and I make four', he should answer 'You and I make five'. If he hears it say 'You and I make six', he should answer 'You and I make seven'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds to the remedy. If the demon answers with an even number, the person always answers with the next odd number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The demon tries to bring the count back to an even number, which is dangerous. The person never lets it end on an even number. He always adds one, so his last word is always odd.

phrases.english: And if he hears a voice saying:
'You and I, that makes four',
phrases.notes: The demon is trying to restore an even number.

phrases.english: let him say to it: 'You and I, that makes five.'
And if he hears it saying:
'You and I, that makes six',
let him say to it: 'You and I, that makes seven.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the remedy of Step 25 to the case where the demon answers back.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Always answer the demon's even number with the next odd number.

steps.title: A story: counting to one hundred and one
steps.stepSummary: There was a case where the counting went up to 101, and the demon burst.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident that went up to one hundred and one, and the demon burst.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. It shows that the counting technique really works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the story, the person kept answering with odd numbers all the way to 101. The demon could not win and burst from frustration. The story supports the remedy described in Steps 25-26.
steps.whatToRemember: The remedy for זוגות is to keep the count odd. Hold your two thumbs and count yourself with them, and always answer the demon's even number with an odd one.

phrases.english: There was an incident
that went up to one hundred and one,
and the demon burst.
phrases.notes: The demon burst in anger because it could not reach an even number.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that shows the counting remedy working.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The odd-count technique defeats the demon.

steps.title: אמימר's formula against witches begins
steps.stepSummary: אמימר reports what the chief of the witches told him: a person who meets witches should say a curse against them. The first lines of the curse appear here.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: The chief of the witches told me: Whoever meets witches should say this: 'Hot dung in torn baskets into your mouths, you witches! May your hair fall out! May your crumbs blow away!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a related topic: protection from witchcraft. אמימר starts quoting a protective curse that he learned from the head of the witches, and the curse continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new protective tool, similar to the remedy against demons above. The words of the curse attack the things witches use for their magic, such as their hair and crumbs. The formula is not finished here.

keyTerms.meaning: may it become bald, may it fall out

steps.confusionAlert: The formula is not finished here. It continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
The chief of the witches told me:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי מַאן דְּפָגַע בְּהוּ בְּנָשִׁים כַּשְׁפָנִיּוֹת,
phrases.english: Whoever encounters witches,
should say as follows:
'Hot dung in torn baskets
into your mouths, you witches!
May your hair fall out,
phrases.notes: They use their hair for witchcraft.

phrases.english: may your crumbs scatter,
phrases.notes: They use crumbs for witchcraft. The formula continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַמֵּימָר: אֲמַרָה לִי רֵישָׁתִינְהִי דְּנָשִׁים כַּשְׁפָנִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from protection against demons to protection against witches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who meets witches should recite a protective curse against them.
